description: Real literature case studies of TCR and peptide mutations for design reference

references.note: Cases compiled from published TCR engineering and peptide design studies

success_cases.rationale: Y→F removed bulky OH group, improved pi-pi stacking geometry with peptide hydrophobic core
lessons: Aromatic substitution works well for pi-pi optimization
Removing H-bond donor is acceptable if not forming critical H-bond
Conservative aromatic changes (Y↔F) are low-risk
success_cases.reference: Robbins et al. 2008, J Immunol; Zhao et al. 2007, J Immunol

success_cases.system: A6 TCR - HTLV-1 Tax peptide LLFGYPVYV / HLA-A*02:01
success_cases.rationale: Improved pi-pi stacking with peptide Tyr; removing OH reduced steric strain
lessons: Aromatic-aromatic contacts benefit from F over Y
CDR3β mutations can maintain specificity
success_cases.reference: Laugel et al. 2007, J Biol Chem

success_cases.system: DMF5 TCR - MART-1 peptide AAGIGILTV / HLA-A*02:01

outcome.reason: Reduced steric clash allowed tighter packing

success_cases.rationale: W was too bulky for the pocket; F provided better fit
lessons: Sometimes reducing aromatic size helps (W→F)
Check steric compatibility before Y→W or F→W

success_cases.system: JM22 TCR - influenza M158-66 peptide GILGFVFTL / HLA-A*02:01
success_cases.rationale: E longer sidechain reduced salt bridge distance, improved geometry
lessons: D→E useful when salt bridge partner is distant (>4 Å)
Measure MD-average distance before designing
success_cases.reference: Analogous to published TCR-HLA optimization studies

success_cases.system: 2B4 TCR - moth cytochrome c peptide / I-Ek
success_cases.rationale: R bidentate H-bond provides stronger, more specific salt bridge than K monodentate
lessons: K→R upgrades salt bridge to bidentate H-bonding
Increased occupancy indicates more stable interaction
success_cases.reference: Analogous to published K→R optimization studies

lessons: L→I conservative substitution for rigid hydrophobic cores
Works best in tight, well-defined pockets

success_cases.system: HIV Gag peptide SLYNTVATL / HLA-A*02:01 (vaccine design)
success_cases.rationale: V better fits HLA-A*02:01 F-pocket (V is preferred anchor along with L, I)
lessons: Anchor optimization can improve MHC binding
HLA-A*02:01 F-pocket prefers V, L, I, M
Always verify with NetMHCpan prediction

success_cases.system: Altered peptide ligand (APL) design for TCR modulation
success_cases.rationale: A→F introduces aromatic for pi-stacking with TCR Tyr; P5 is TCR-contact position with high tolerance
lessons: P4-P6 positions tolerate aromatic substitutions well
Enhancing TCR contact can boost immunogenicity
Must verify MHC binding is maintained

failure_cases.rationale: Framework position is buried in hydrophobic core; L→A removed critical packing contacts
lessons: Avoid framework mutations - they support structural integrity
Even conservative hydrophobic reduction (L→A) can destabilize
Framework positions identified by low RMSF (<1 Å) and high conservation

outcome.reason: Broke salt bridge with peptide Glu, introduced same-charge repulsion

failure_cases.rationale: Charge reversal destroys electrostatic interactions and can introduce repulsion
lessons: Never reverse charge (R→E, K→D, E→R, D→K)
Conservative: R↔K, E↔D are safe
Identify charge partner before mutating

outcome.reason: Proline rigidified CDR3 loop, disrupted induced fit

failure_cases.rationale: CDR3 loops require flexibility for peptide recognition; Pro restricts backbone conformation
lessons: Never introduce Proline into CDR loops
Pro restricts phi angle to ~-60°
Breaks H-bond donor capability of backbone NH

outcome.reason: G provides critical flexibility at tight turn; A restricts phi/psi

failure_cases.rationale: Glycine's unique lack of sidechain allows backbone conformations forbidden to other residues
lessons: Don't remove Glycine from tight turns
Check phi/psi space before G→other substitutions
Safe: G in helix or sheet regions can sometimes be replaced

failure_cases.rationale: HLA-A*02:01 B-pocket is hydrophobic; requires L, I, V, M, A at P2. Introducing charged E destroys binding
lessons: Never mutate anchor positions to non-preferred residues
HLA-A*02:01 P2: L > I > V > M > A
HLA-A*02:01 PΩ: V, L, I, M
Always check NetMHCpan before peptide design

failure_cases.rationale: Over-optimization of affinity (>100x) can cause loss of specificity and T cell dysfunction
lessons: Target 5-50x improvement, not >1000x
Monitor cross-reactivity with peptide libraries
Supra-physiological affinities cause T cell exhaustion
Clinical failures have occurred due to off-target effects
failure_cases.reference: MAGE-A3 TCR clinical trial outcomes (Cameron et al. 2013, Sci Transl Med)

best_practices: Consider steric constraints before Y→W or F→W
Avoid if charge partner is transient (occupancy < 50%)
Only change to preferred HLA motif residues
Always verify with NetMHCpan (target KD < 500 nM)
HLA-A*02:01 P2: prefer L, I, V, M
HLA-A*02:01 PΩ: prefer V, L, I, M

common_pitfalls.mitigation: Always extract MD-average distance, angle, occupancy before designing

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Ignoring steric constraints in small→large substitutions
common_pitfalls.mitigation: Check pocket volume before Y→W, F→W, A→L

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Focusing only on affinity, not specificity
common_pitfalls.mitigation: Test against peptide variants; limit improvement to 50x

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Not verifying MHC binding for peptide mutants
common_pitfalls.mitigation: Always run NetMHCpan after peptide design

common_pitfalls.pitfall: Attempting multi-point mutations without single-point data
common_pitfalls.mitigation: Test each mutation individually first, then combine top hits
